title: A calf of their own gold that could not say a word.
subtitle: Worshipping what they made with their own hands
then: While Musa was at his appointment, As-Samiri made a calf from the ornaments the people had borrowed, and it seemed to low. Ibn Kathir says people {trap}danced around it and said this is your god and the god of Musa{/trap}. The verse asks: did they not see it could neither speak to them nor guide them?
now: Your salary, your follower count, your reputation. You built them with your own effort, and now they set your mood each morning. {trap}They make a lot of noise.{/trap} {idea}But not one of them can tell you how to live or carry you through death.{/idea}
old: What I built with my own hands is what I can depend on.
new: Anything that cannot guide me does not deserve my devotion, however much it shines.
try: Name one thing you made that you now serve. Spend today using it, not obeying it.

title: When regret came, they said: without His mercy we are lost.
subtitle: The first honest step back
then: After worshipping the calf, the people felt deep regret and saw they had gone astray. They said that if their Lord did not have mercy on them and forgive them, they would be lost. Ibn Kathir calls this {reward}their recognition of their sin and their way of seeking salvation from Allah{/reward}.
now: You wake up the morning after saying something cruel. The shame sits heavy. You can spiral into how bad you are, or you can say: {reward}Ya Allah, I was wrong, forgive me.{/reward} One leads nowhere. The other leads back.
old: After what I did, there is no point asking.
new: Regret is meant to turn me toward Allah's mercy, not away from it.
try: Think of one thing you regret. Say this verse's words as a dua: if You do not forgive me, I am lost.

title: Seeing it with his own eyes, Musa threw down the Tablets.
subtitle: Anger for Allah's sake, and a brother's plea
then: Musa returned angry and grieved. Ibn Kathir cites the Prophet ﷺ: {idea}information is not like seeing{/idea}. Allah had told Musa about the calf, but he only threw the Tablets when he saw it. He grabbed Harun, fearing he had not tried hard enough. Harun said: {trap}the people overpowered me and almost killed me{/trap}.
now: You come home and the kitchen is a mess, the kids are on screens, and you turn on your partner before asking a single question. {idea}Anger for the right reason can still land on the wrong person.{/idea} Hear their side first.
old: When I am angry for a good reason, I am allowed to react.
new: Even righteous anger needs to listen before it blames.
try: Next time you walk into a situation that angers you, ask one question before you say anything else.

title: Forgive me and my brother, Most Merciful of the merciful.
subtitle: Musa's first words after his anger cooled

row.title: pray for us both
sub: me and the one I hurt

then: When Musa was satisfied his brother was innocent, Ibn Kathir says, citing 20:90, that Harun had warned the people they were being tested. Musa then prayed: {reward}My Lord, forgive me and my brother, and admit us into Your mercy{/reward}. He began with himself.
now: After a heated fight with your sibling, you find out they were not to blame. You could quietly move on. Or you could say sorry, and in your sujud that night ask Allah to {reward}forgive you both{/reward}.
old: Once I find out I was wrong, it is easier to just drop it.
new: Repair starts with asking forgiveness for myself and praying for the one I hurt.
try: Make dua tonight for someone you were harsh with recently. Name them in it.

title: Inventing falsehood about Allah carries its own disgrace.
subtitle: The consequence of the calf, and of every invented lie
then: The verse says those who took the calf would meet anger from their Lord and humiliation in this life. Abu Qilabah said: {idea}by Allah, this ayah is for all who invent a lie, until the Day of Resurrection{/idea}. Sufyan bin 'Uyaynah said every person who invents in religion will taste disgrace.
now: It is easy to make up a rule about religion that suits your mood, or to repeat something as from the Prophet ﷺ without checking. {trap}Inventing about Allah is heavy.{/trap} {idea}Saying I do not know is safer.{/idea}
old: It is fine to say what I think religion means, it is just my opinion.
new: Speaking about Allah without knowledge is serious, so I check before I speak.
try: Before you forward the next religious quote, check its source first. If you cannot, do not send it.

title: Whatever you did, after repentance your Lord forgives.
subtitle: The door that stays open, even after the calf
then: Right after the warning about the calf comes this promise. Ibn Kathir says {reward}Allah accepts repentance for any sin, even shirk, disbelief and hypocrisy{/reward}. He notes the verse addresses the Prophet ﷺ, the messenger of repentance and mercy.
now: You have a list in your head of things you did that you think Allah could never let go: the years without prayer, the lies, the person you hurt. {reward}The verse says: after all that, your Lord is Forgiving.{/reward} The word after matters.
old: Some things I did are too big for Allah to forgive.
new: No sin is bigger than Allah's forgiveness for someone who turns back.
try: Pray two rak'ahs tonight with the intention of repentance. Ask for one specific thing to be forgiven.

title: When his anger quieted, Musa picked the Tablets back up.
subtitle: Guidance and mercy, waiting after the storm
then: Musa had thrown the Tablets out of anger for Allah's sake. When the anger subsided, {idea}he took them up again{/idea}. In them was guidance and mercy for those who fear their Lord. Ibn Kathir mentions reports that they had broken, adding that only Allah knows if those reports are true.
now: You slammed the Quran app shut after a bad day, or stopped praying for a week after an argument. The anger has passed now. {reward}The guidance is still there, waiting for you to pick it up.{/reward}
old: I dropped it in a bad moment, so I have lost it.
new: When the anger settles, I can pick up guidance again and find mercy in it.
try: If you put down a good habit in a hard moment, pick it back up today, in a small way.

title: You are our Protector, so forgive us and have mercy.
subtitle: Musa's plea when the seventy were struck
then: Musa took seventy men to the appointment to seek forgiveness for the calf. Reports in Ibn Kathir say they demanded to see Allah, or did not forbid their people. {trap}They were seized by a tremor.{/trap} Musa did not argue. He said this was {idea}Allah's trial{/idea}, and asked: You are our Protector, so forgive us.
now: Something hits your whole family at once: a layoff, a diagnosis, a loss. You want to ask why us. {idea}Musa's words show another way{/idea}: this is a test, You are in charge, You are our Wali, forgive and have mercy on us.
old: When something bad hits us, it means Allah has turned against us.
new: A trial is from Allah, and the answer is to turn to Him as our Protector.
try: In your next dua, say: Anta waliyyuna faghfir lana warhamna. Mean it for your whole household.

title: My mercy embraces all things, says Allah.
subtitle: Asking for good in both worlds, and the answer
then: Musa asked Allah for good in this world and the next, saying: we have turned back to You. Ibn Kathir says hudna means {idea}we repent and return to You{/idea}. Allah replied that His {reward}mercy embraces all things{/reward}, and He will write it for those who are mindful of Him, give zakah, and believe in His signs.
now: You are in the waiting room, scared, feeling like you have no right to ask for anything. {reward}Mercy that covers everything covers this room too.{/reward} Ask for the good of this life and the next, and turn back to Him while you ask.
old: Allah's mercy is for people better than me.
new: His mercy covers all things, and I can step into it by turning back to Him.
try: Say this dua today: Rabbana atina fid-dunya hasanah wa fil-akhirati hasanah.

title: The Prophet ﷺ came to lift the heavy burdens.
subtitle: Mercy written for those who follow the unlettered Prophet
then: This answers who the mercy of 7:156 is for: those who follow the unlettered Prophet ﷺ, described in earlier scriptures. Ibn Kathir says {reward}he came with leniency and an easy religion{/reward}, citing his words: I was sent with the easy way of pure monotheism, and his advice to make things easy, not difficult.
now: Maybe you feel religion as a list you keep failing. Too many rules, too much guilt. {reward}The Prophet ﷺ was sent to take shackles off, not add them.{/reward} Following him starts with that lightness.
old: Being religious means carrying a heavy load.
new: Following the Prophet ﷺ is a release from heavy burdens, not a new one.
try: Next time someone asks you about Islam, share one thing that makes life easier, not harder.

title: I am the Messenger of Allah to you all.
subtitle: A message for every person, everywhere
then: The Prophet ﷺ is told to say he is Allah's Messenger to all people. Ibn Kathir says this is {idea}directed to mankind, red and black, Arab and non-Arab alike{/idea}. He cites Abu Bakr's moment: when others said you lie, Abu Bakr said you speak the truth.
now: You sometimes feel the message is for the people at the masjid who know Arabic, who grew up with it. {idea}The Prophet ﷺ said: to you all.{/idea} That includes you on your commute, at your desk, wherever you are.
old: This message is for people more religious than me.
new: The Prophet ﷺ was sent to me as much as to anyone.
try: Read one hadith today as if the Prophet ﷺ were saying it directly to you.
